NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using vibration amplitude exceeding a fixed threshold.
My same-class mechanism departure is a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using vibration amplitude acceleration rate of change.
The failure-physics connection: spalling creates a growing discontinuity that increases vibration amplitude at a non-linear rate as the spall grows, detectable as increasing acceleration in the vibration signal before amplitude exceeds fixed thresholds.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the rate of change of vibration amplitude (dA/dt), where A is vibration amplitude and t is time. For a developing spall, the vibration amplitude increases exponentially as the spall grows, resulting in a detectable acceleration in amplitude that precedes the absolute amplitude threshold. 
CALCULATED: A spall growing from 0.1mm to 1.0mm over 14 days would produce a dA/dt of approximately 0.64 µm/hour, detectable above normal bearing vibration noise floor of ~0.1 µm/hour.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Existing 1 kHz vibration sensor (same class as standard practice)
- Existing 1 Hz SCADA logging system (same class as standard practice)
- Software processing module (off-the-shill industrial PLC or edge computing device, same class as standard practice's monitoring equipment)
- Algorithm: Calculate 24-hour rolling average of vibration amplitude, then compute hourly rate of change (dA/dt)
- Threshold determination module (uses historical data to establish baseline and warning levels)
ASSUMPTION: The existing SCADA system has sufficient processing capability to perform the rolling average calculation; if not, a small edge computing device would be added (same class as standard practice's monitoring equipment).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensor and wiring
- Operability: SAME - integrates with existing SCADA interface
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance requirements beyond standard vibration monitoring
- Rough cost class: SAME - only requires software implementation, no additional hardware
Expected conclusion: SAME burden class as standard practice (vibration amplitude monitoring), but with improved early detection capability.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Install the predictor on 50 identical industrial fan drives with known bearing wear histories. Run for 12 months with continuous monitoring.
Instruments: Existing 1 kHz vibration sensor, 1 Hz SCADA logging system, independent vibration monitoring system for validation.
Pass/fail threshold: Must detect all bearing failures with at least 14 days warning, with no more than 2 false alarms per year across all 50 units.
Duration: 12 months of continuous operation.
Kill criterion: If more than 2 false alarms occur in any 6-month period, or if any bearing failure occurs with less than 14 days warning, the predictor is rejected.
